clue.text: Rude person around middle of programme coming in and presenting item one shouldn't miss?

indicators.note: the rude person's word is wrapped around what follows, so it sits outside the rest

parts.note: a boor is a rude, ill-mannered person

indicators.note: the middle letter enters the word 'and', so it is placed inside it

parts.note: the word 'and' used as written

indicators.note: the centre letter of the nine-letter word programme is wanted

explanation.surface: A rude man barges in midway through a show, carrying something nobody could fail to notice.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the saying that a poor shot 'couldn't hit a barn door', the target being so big.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who cannot 'hit a barn door' is a hopeless shot, since the target is so large it should never be missed.

clue.text: Shot showing counter

definitions.meaning: in golf, a short lofted stroke onto the green
a gambling token used in place of money

explanation.definitionFit: A short lofted golf stroke and a casino gaming token share the one name.

clue.text: Attitude expressed by number in musical put over with energy

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting a word over turns it to read upwards
the number letter is placed inside the musical's name

parts.note: Cats is the Andrew Lloyd Webber musical
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A stance is shown by a song from a stage show delivered with vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: N goes into CATS to give CNATS, and 'put over' turns that upwards to STANC; E finishes. 'Number in musical' looks like a song from a show.
explanation.definitionFit: A stance is a mental position or point of view taken on something.

clue.text: Truce broken by a king with entirely apparent change of position

indicators.note: the truce word is split open so that other letters are put inside it

parts.note: pax is Latin for peace and a schoolchild's call for a truce
R is short for rex, Latin for king
all means wholly or entirely

explanation.surface: A peace deal is shattered by a monarch, wholly changing his stance.
explanation.walkthrough: The inserted pieces go in after the truce word's first letter, splitting it as P...AX.
explanation.definitionFit: Parallax is the seeming shift of an object against its background when viewed from a different spot.

clue.text: Mischief-maker associated with pieces suppressed by censor with difficulty

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous little devil

indicators.note: the pieces are held down inside the censor's word, so they go within it

parts.note: to censor a text is to edit it
men are the pieces in chess or draughts

explanation.surface: A troublemaker's work is cut by the censor, who finds it hard going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pieces' are chessmen, so MEN; 'suppressed' puts them inside the censor's word.
explanation.definitionFit: An impediment is an obstacle or hindrance, something that makes progress hard.

clue.text: Belabour blockhead over trouble

indicators.note: in a down clue, a word over another is written above it, so it comes first

parts.note: an ass is a fool or dolt
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: Beat up a dimwit because of some bother.
explanation.definitionFit: To belabour someone is to attack them hard, with blows or with words.

clue.text: Poor president, disbelieving, is ousted

indicators.note: the word 'is' is thrown out of the longer word, so those letters are removed

parts.note: atheistic describes someone who does not believe in a god
the letters of 'is' as written

explanation.surface: A sorry head of state, losing his faith, is thrown out of office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'President' looks like part of the surface's subject but gives only its abbreviation; 'is ousted' removes those two letters from the disbelieving word.
explanation.definitionFit: Pathetic means pitifully inadequate, as in a weak or feeble effort.

clue.text: Strike about to end

definitions.meaning: to strike out or sever, as a supply is stopped
to bring something to a sudden stop

explanation.surface: A walk-out is about to finish.
explanation.definitionFit: To sever a supply or strike something out is to stop it; a phone call can also be stopped short this way.

clue.text: Line in book that's first? Not quite

indicators.note: the line letter is placed inside the book's name

parts.note: Amos is a book of the Old Testament

indicators.note: only the opening letter of 'that's' is taken

explanation.surface: A verse in the opening book of the Bible? Not exactly.
explanation.walkthrough: L goes into AMOS to make ALMOS, and the first letter of 'that's' adds T. 'Book that's first' looks like Genesis, but 'first' belongs to 'that's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Almost means nearly but not entirely.

clue.text: Second choice of tipster in photograph

parts.note: a nap is a racing tipster's most confident selection

explanation.surface: A tipster's runner-up pick appears in a picture.
explanation.walkthrough: A NAP is the British racing tipster's best bet of the day.
explanation.definitionFit: A snap is an informal snapshot taken quickly with a camera.

clue.text: Tranquilliser? Chap lies back, having swallowed it, level and quiet

indicators.note: the reversed word takes the other letters inside it, like food swallowed
the chap's word lies the other way round, so it is read backwards

parts.note: a man is a chap
the word as written
to raze a building is to level it to the ground
p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: A man lies back in a calm, flat silence after taking a sedative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lies back' turns the chap round to NAM; the rest goes between its N and AM. The question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitrazepam is a benzodiazepine drug prescribed as a sedative and sleeping pill.

clue.text: Writer capturing sorry state of old lackey

indicators.note: the writer's name holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe, the American writer

indicators.note: the word old is in a poor, broken condition, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An author takes in the poor condition of an ancient servant.
explanation.walkthrough: OLD in a 'sorry state' becomes ODL, captured in POE.
explanation.definitionFit: A poodle is a servile follower who does another's bidding, like a fawning pet dog.

clue.text: Shabby party spin? Brown, upset, goes into it

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration

indicators.note: the turned colour word enters the spin word, so it sits inside it

parts.note: to wheel is to spin round

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns the word upside down so it reads backwards

parts.note: tan is a shade of brown

explanation.surface: A scruffy party where the host, Brown, falls over while spinning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' turns the colour to NAT; 'it' points back to the spin word, which the turned colour goes into after its W.
explanation.definitionFit: Down at heel describes someone whose clothes are worn out and who looks poor and seedy.

clue.text: Human turning bad in story

indicators.note: the turned word sits inside the story word

parts.note: a fable is a short moral story

indicators.note: the word for bad turns round, so it is read in reverse

parts.note: ill means bad, as in ill luck

explanation.surface: A person goes wrong in a tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning' reverses the word for bad, and 'in' places it after the story word's first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To be human is to be prone to error, as in 'to err is human'.

clue.text: Get absorbed by revolutionary function of tape recorder

indicators.note: the getting word is soaked up inside the revolutionary word

parts.note: red is the colour and label of a communist revolutionary
to win something is to get it

explanation.surface: Getting caught up in the spinning function of an old cassette machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary' hints at spinning reels but means a Red, the communist label.
explanation.definitionFit: Rewinding runs the tape backwards to its start on a cassette or reel-to-reel machine.

clue.text: Knotty swelling in gnarled wood's tiny, not wide

indicators.note: gnarled means twisted and knotted, so the letters are twisted into a new order
the letter for wide is to be left out of the words

parts.note: the word as written, its apostrophe giving no letter
the word as written
W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide

explanation.surface: A knotty growth on twisted timber is small, and narrow.
explanation.walkthrough: WOODS TINY without W leaves OODSTINY, which 'gnarled' rearranges. A wide is a cricket ball bowled out of the batter's reach.
explanation.definitionFit: Nodosity is the state of having knots or nodes, or such a knobbly lump itself.

clue.text: Authority to use overwhelming power

indicators.note: the word for using covers the power letter completely, holding it inside

parts.note: to exert pressure is to use or apply it
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: Someone in charge is free to wield crushing force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overwhelming' signals a container: the power letter goes within the word for using.
explanation.definitionFit: An expert is a specialist whose knowledge makes them an authority on a subject.

clue.text: Material, referring to birth, despicable person raised

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the pieces are read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: natal means relating to birth
a rat is a contemptible, disloyal person

explanation.surface: Cloth, concerning a birth, brought up by a nasty person.
explanation.walkthrough: NATAL + RAT read upwards gives TAR + LATAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarlatan is a thin, stiff open-weave muslin fabric used for ball gowns and stage costumes.

clue.text: Schism created by bishop going on strike

indicators.note: in a down clue, the bishop letter goes on top of the other word

parts.note: B is the chess notation for bishop
to reach a target is to strike or hit it

explanation.surface: A church split caused by a bishop walking out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strike' suggests industrial action, but it means REACH, as in to arrive at or hit.
explanation.definitionFit: A breach is a break in relations, a rift between parties.

clue.text: One who has key for home?

definitions.text: One who has key for home?

parts.words: One who has key for home?
parts.note: the key is a low coral island or cay, not a door key, so this is someone whose home is on such an islet

explanation.definitionFit: An islander lives on an island, and a key (cay) is a small island.

clue.text: Star with range of knowledge that's low

parts.note: the sun is our star
ken means the range of one's knowledge, as in 'beyond my ken'

explanation.surface: A celebrity with a broad understanding that is beneath them.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunken means lying below the surrounding level, as in a sunken garden.

clue.text: Elect to yield

definitions.meaning: to choose a candidate by vote, as a constituency does its MP
to produce a profit or income

explanation.definitionFit: A constituency sends its chosen MP to Parliament, and an investment gives a profit; both share one verb.

clue.text: Upset artist right to have one thrown out?

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts

indicators.note: 'to have ... thrown out' frames the letter for one as something the right word must lose
the letter for one is expelled from the word for right, so it is removed

parts.note: a title is a legal right, as to property
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An artist is upset that his right to have someone expelled is challenged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right' is a noun here, a legal title, not a direction; RA is the usual crossword artist.
explanation.definitionFit: To rattle someone is to unnerve or disconcert them.

clue.text: Entertaining us, eccentric sat in the buff

indicators.note: entertaining means holding as a guest, so the anagram holds the other letters within it
eccentric means odd or out of line, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word as written

explanation.surface: Amusing us, a weirdo sat naked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eccentric' rearranges SAT IN THE, and 'Entertaining' has that result hold US. 'In the buff' looks like naked, but 'buff' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A buff is a keen fan, as in a film buff.

clue.text: You're going to jumble sale to get plug?

indicators.note: to jumble things is to mix them up, so the letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Off to a jumble sale to find a stopper for the sink?
explanation.walkthrough: A jumble sale is a British charity sale of second-hand goods; here 'jumble' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A seal is something that stops a gap or opening, as a stopper does.

clue.text: Story appearing in papers again

indicators.note: the answer shows up inside the run of letters of the next words

explanation.surface: A tale printed in the newspapers once more.
explanation.definitionFit: A saga is a long story, originally an Old Norse prose tale of heroes and families.

clue.text: Hate time after time getting lapped by leading competitor running round

indicators.note: the first time letter is placed after the rest
the second time letter is surrounded by the competitor's word, as a runner is lapped
the competitor's word goes round the other way, so it is read in reverse

parts.note: a seed is a top-ranked player in a tournament

explanation.surface: Loathing being overtaken again and again by the frontrunner on the track.
explanation.walkthrough: SEED read in reverse is DEES; T goes inside it to make DETES, and the other T follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To detest is to loathe or abhor.
